core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aaron is the English form of the Hebrew name אַהֲרֹן (Aharon); its original etymology is uncertain.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: A traditional Hebrew personal name; no single etymology is asserted as settled.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The English name Aaron represents Hebrew אַהֲרֹן (Aharon). Its etymology is disputed, so “mountain of strength” should not be stated as a verified literal meaning. The related Arabic name هارون (Hārūn) is the Qur'anic name of the prophet Harun; Aaron and Hārūn are related traditional forms but not the same script form.

origin.origin_explanation: Aaron is the English form associated with Hebrew אַהֲרֹן (Aharon). In Islamic scripture the related Arabic form is هارون (Hārūn). The two forms should not be conflated when describing language or transliteration.

religion.primary_association: Biblical and Islamic scriptural traditions through related forms

religion.religious_explanation: Aaron is the English/Hebrew form associated with the prophet known in Arabic as Hārūn (هارون), who is mentioned in the Qur'an. The English spelling Aaron itself is not the Arabic Qur'anic spelling.

quranic_status.note: The English/Hebrew form Aaron is not the Qur'anic Arabic spelling; the related Arabic form Hārūn (هارون) is named in the Qur'an.

prophetic_status.note: The prophet Aaron is known in the Qur'an by the Arabic form Hārūn (هارون). Do not claim that the English spelling Aaron is the Arabic form used in the Qur'an.

faq.a: Aaron is the English form associated with Hebrew אַהֲרֹן (Aharon). Its etymology is disputed, so “mountain of strength” is not treated as a verified meaning.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aaron?
faq.a: The English name Aaron is associated with Hebrew Aharon. The related Arabic form is Hārūn (هارون).
Aaron is not an Arabic spelling. The Arabic form of the related prophetic name is هارون (Hārūn).

faq.q: What is the root of Aaron?
faq.a: No Hebrew root analysis or single settled etymology is asserted for Aaron in this record.
Aaron is used in Jewish and Christian contexts; the related form Hārūn is also important in Islam. Language forms should be kept distinct.
The English spelling Aaron is not the Arabic spelling used in the Qur'an; the related Arabic name Hārūn (هارون) is mentioned in the Qur'an.

faq.q: What does Aaron mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the related Arabic form is written ہارون. The record does not assign “mountain of strength” as a verified Urdu meaning.
“AIR-un” or “AA-ron” vary by English accent; the record's romanized approximation is not a universal pronunciation.

faq.q: Is Aaron a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Aaron is traditionally masculine in English naming usage; naming conventions may vary across cultures.
